'''Musashi-Mitake Shrine''' (武蔵御嶽神社) is a Shinto shrine located on the summit of {{ill|Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|ja|武蔵御岳山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Mitake (Tokyo)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|Ōme, Tokyo|en|Ōme, Tokyo|qid=Q237683|lt=Ōme, Tokyo|1=Ōme, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, formerly within Tama District, {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province|1=Musashi Province}}.
"Mitake" refers to {{ill|Mount Kinpu|ja|金峯山|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mount Kinpu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 金峰山|1=Mount Kinpusen|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10563986}} in Yoshino, Nara Prefecture, a central site of Shugendo. It enshrines {{ill|Zaō Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaō Gongen|qq=}} and Kushimachi-no-Mikoto, becoming significant as a mountain worship site since medieval times, with influence in Musashi and Sagami. Some theories identify it as the Shikinai Shrine "Ōmato no Zu Ten Shrine" (see {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Musashi Province|ja|武蔵国の式内社一覧|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/List of Shikinaisha in Musashi Province|qq=}}). It is currently an independent shrine, not affiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|Association of Shinto Shrines|qid=Q908077|lt=Association of Shinto Shrines|1=Association of Shinto Shrines}}.
Due to its enshrinement of {{ill|Ōkuchi Magami|ja|大口真神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuchi Magami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 真神|1=Ōkuchi no Magami|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2349235}} (dog deity), it attracts visitors bringing dogs for prayer. The {{ill|Mitake Tozan Railway|en|Mitake Tozan Railway|qid=Q6880754|lt=Mitake Tozan Railway|1=Mitake Tozan Railway}} allows dogs without cages.

== History ==
Founded traditionally in 91 BC (7th year of Emperor Sujin), it is said Gyōki invited Zaō Gongen in 736. In 1234, Ōnakatomi no Kunika restored it from ruin, and it later became popular among samurai, receiving weapon donations. During the Edo period, in 1605, it was rebuilt under Ōkubo Nagayasu's supervision. It was renamed from Mitake Daigongen to "Ōmato no Zu Ten Shrine" after the Meiji-era Shinto-Buddhist separation, later adopting "Mitake Shrine" and finally "Musashi-Mitake Shrine" in 1952.
== Grounds and structures ==
[[File:武蔵御岳神社_本殿.jpg|thumb|200px|Honden]]
;Main Shrine
:Single-bay Shinmei-zukuri built in 1877. Holds Zaō Gongen statue shown every 12 years.
;Other shrines on-site:
* Futahashira Shrine (Izanagi, Izanami)
* Yahashira Shrine (Kasuga, Hachiman, etc.)
* Kitano Shrine (Sugawara no Michizane)
* Kofuku Shrine (Haniyasuhime)
* Shinmei Shrine (Amaterasu)
* Ōkuchi Magami Shrine (wolf deity)
* Tokiwakakiwa Shrine (Emperors Sujin, Keikō, Ankan, Seiwa, etc., Tokyo-designated cultural property)
* Sumemimanomikoto Shrine (Ninigi-no-Mikoto)
* Tōshō Shrine (Tokugawa Ieyasu)
* Treasure Hall (holds national treasures like armor)
* Hatakeyama Shigetada Statue
* Okumiya (Yamato Takeru)
* Ubuyasu Shrine (Konohanasakuyahime, etc., fertility shrine)
* Zuishin Gate
* Inari Shrine
== Festivals ==
*New Year's, Setsubun, Spring Festival, Sunrise Festival, Great Purification, Yabusame Festival (September 29, symbolic ritual without horses), Autumn Festival.
== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
*Red-thread-laced armor with helmet (donated by Hatakeyama Shigetada, late Heian)
*Circular-pattern raden saddle set (Kamakura)
=== Important Cultural Properties ===
*Purple-gradient armor (mid-Kamakura)
*Gilt-edged tachi sword (Kamakura)
*Black lacquer scabbard tachi sword marked "Hōju"
== Access ==
From JR Ome Line Mitake Station, bus to Cable Shita stop (10 min), Mitake Tozan Railway to Mt. Mitake station (6 min), 25 min walk to the shrine. Paid parking available at Takimoto station.
